es.summary: Trastorno neurológico caracterizado por una necesidad irresistible de mover las piernas, que empeora en reposo y al anochecer, y se alivia temporalmente con el movimiento.
key_points: Empeora al estar sentado o acostado y mejora con la actividad.
Frecuente causa de insomnio y somnolencia diurna.
Puede estar asociado a deficiencia de hierro, embarazo o neuropatías.
El diagnóstico es clínico; se descarta otras causas de inquietud.
El tratamiento incluye corrección de hierro y fármacos dopaminérgicos.

pathophysiology: Disfunción de la dopamina en el sistema nervioso central.
Alteración del control sensitivo‑motor de las extremidades inferiores.
Hipoxia cerebral parcial y déficit de hierro que afecta la síntesis de dopamina.
risk_factors: Embarazo, insuficiencia renal crónica y neuropatías periféricas.
Uso de fármacos que antagonizan la dopamina (antipsicóticos, antieméticos).
Consumo excesivo de cafeína, alcohol o tabaco.
signs_symptoms: Urgencia de mover las piernas acompañada de hormigueo, ardor o dolor.
Síntomas que aparecen al reposo, especialmente al anochecer.
Alivio parcial o total con el movimiento de piernas o estiramiento.
Despertares nocturnos y dificultad para conciliar el sueño.
diagnostics: Historia clínica enfocada en los criterios de International Restless Legs Study Group.
Examen físico y neurológico para excluir neuropatías.
Laboratorio: ferritina sérica, hierro y capacidad total de fijación del hierro.
Polisomnografía o estudio de movimientos de piernas si se sospecha PLMD.
treatment: Suplementación de hierro oral o intravenosa cuando ferritina < 50 ng/mL.
Gabapentina o pregabalina en casos de intolerancia dopaminérgica.
Modificaciones del estilo de vida: higiene del sueño, ejercicio moderado, evitar cafeína/alcohol.
complications: Privación de sueño crónica y somnolencia diurna.
Fatiga, disminución del rendimiento académico o laboral.
Trastornos del estado de ánimo (ansiedad, depresión).
Aumento del riesgo de caídas por movimientos nocturnos.
nursing_care: Evaluar la intensidad del impulso y su impacto en el sueño (escala de 0‑10).
Monitorear niveles de ferritina y respuesta a la suplementación de hierro.
Registrar patrones de sueño y episodios de movimiento nocturno.
Promover posición cómoda, uso de almohadas y técnicas de relajación antes de dormir.
Observar efectos adversos de fármacos dopaminérgicos (náuseas, alucinaciones).
patient_teaching: Mantener una rutina de sueño regular y ambiente oscuro y silencioso.
Limitar cafeína, alcohol y tabaco, especialmente en la tarde.
Realizar estiramientos de piernas y ejercicio moderado durante el día.
Tomar suplementos de hierro según indicación y evitar tomarlo con lácteos o té.
Informar al profesional de salud sobre cualquier empeoramiento o efectos secundarios de la medicación.

related_to: dolor o incomodidad al estar en reposo
evidenced_by: inquietud al estar sentado o acostado
outcomes: Nivel de actividad: mantener actividad tolerable durante el día (escala 0‑10 ≤ 3)
Calidad del sueño: lograr 6‑8 h de sueño continuo

interventions.action: Evaluar la intensidad del impulso de mover piernas cada turno usando escala de 0‑10
interventions.rationale: Permite cuantificar la gravedad y monitorizar la respuesta al tratamiento

interventions.action: Registrar patrones de sueño y despertares nocturnos en hoja de observación
interventions.rationale: Facilita la identificación de deterioro del sueño y la efectividad de intervenciones

interventions.action: Enseñar ejercicios de estiramiento de piernas antes de acostarse
interventions.rationale: Reduce la sensación de incomodidad y disminuye la necesidad de movimiento

interventions.action: Promover higiene del sueño (horario regular, ambiente oscuro)
interventions.rationale: Mejora la consolidación del sueño y disminuye la frecuencia de episodios

interventions.action: Monitorear niveles de ferritina y administrar suplementos de hierro según prescripción
interventions.rationale: La deficiencia de hierro está asociada a mayor intensidad del síndrome

outcomes: Patrón de sueño: lograr 6‑8 h de sueño continuo sin despertares >2 veces por noche
Estado de alerta: reportar nivel de energía ≥ 7/10 durante el día

interventions.action: Implementar rutina de relajación (respiración profunda, música suave) antes de acostarse
interventions.rationale: Reduce la excitación del sistema nervioso y facilita el inicio del sueño

interventions.action: Limitar consumo de cafeína y alcohol después de las 14:00 h
interventions.rationale: Estas sustancias pueden exacerbar los síntomas del SPI y alterar el sueño

interventions.action: Fomentar actividad física moderada (30 min) al menos 3 veces/semana
interventions.rationale: El ejercicio regular mejora la calidad del sueño y disminuye la intensidad del SPI

interventions.action: Revisar y registrar efectos secundarios de los fármacos dopaminérgicos (ej. somnolencia diurna)
interventions.rationale: Permite ajustar la terapia para optimizar el sueño sin causar sedación excesiva

interventions.action: Coordinar con el médico la posible ajuste de medicación si los episodios persisten
interventions.rationale: Ajustes farmacológicos pueden ser necesarios para controlar el SPI y mejorar el sueño

en.summary: A neurological disorder characterized by an irresistible urge to move the legs, worsening at rest and in the evening, and temporarily relieved by movement.
key_points: Worsens when sitting or lying down and improves with activity.
Common cause of insomnia and daytime sleepiness.
May be associated with iron deficiency, pregnancy, or neuropathies.
Diagnosis is clinical; other causes of restlessness are excluded.
Treatment includes iron correction and dopaminergic medications.

pathophysiology: Dopamine dysfunction in the central nervous system.
Altered sensorimotor control of the lower extremities.
Partial cerebral hypoxia and iron deficiency affecting dopamine synthesis.
risk_factors: Pregnancy, chronic kidney disease, and peripheral neuropathies.
Excessive consumption of caffeine, alcohol, or tobacco.
signs_symptoms: Urgency to move the legs accompanied by tingling, burning, or pain.
Symptoms appear at rest, especially at dusk.
Partial or total relief with leg movement or stretching.
Nocturnal awakenings and difficulty falling asleep.
diagnostics: Focused history on International Restless Legs Study Group criteria.
Physical and neurological exam to exclude neuropathies.
Laboratory: serum ferritin, iron, and total iron-binding capacity.
Polysomnography or leg movement study if PLMD is suspected.
treatment: Oral or intravenous iron supplementation when ferritin < 50 ng/mL.
Gabapentin or pregabalin for dopaminergic intolerance.
Lifestyle modifications: sleep hygiene, moderate exercise, avoid caffeine/alcohol.
complications: Chronic sleep deprivation and daytime sleepiness.
Fatigue, reduced academic or work performance.
Increased fall risk from nighttime movements.
nursing_care: Assess the intensity of the urge and its impact on sleep (0‑10 scale).
Monitor ferritin levels and response to iron supplementation.
Document sleep patterns and nighttime movement episodes.
Promote a comfortable position, use pillows, and relaxation techniques before sleep.
Observe adverse effects of dopaminergic drugs (nausea, hallucinations).
patient_teaching: Maintain a regular sleep routine in a dark, quiet environment.
Limit caffeine, alcohol, and tobacco, especially in the afternoon.
Perform leg stretches and moderate exercise during the day.
Take iron supplements as prescribed and avoid dairy or tea with them.
Report any worsening or medication side effects to the healthcare provider.

evidenced_by: restlessness when sitting or lying down
outcomes: Activity level: maintain tolerable activity during the day (0‑10 ≤ 3)
Sleep quality: achieve 6‑8 h of continuous sleep

interventions.action: Assess the intensity of the urge to move legs each shift using a 0‑10 scale
interventions.rationale: Allows quantification of severity and monitoring of treatment response

interventions.action: Record sleep patterns and nighttime awakenings on an observation sheet
interventions.rationale: Facilitates identification of sleep deterioration and intervention effectiveness

interventions.action: Teach leg stretching exercises before bedtime
interventions.rationale: Reduces discomfort and decreases the need for movement

interventions.action: Promote sleep hygiene (regular schedule, dark environment)
interventions.rationale: Improves sleep consolidation and reduces episode frequency

interventions.action: Monitor ferritin levels and administer iron supplements as prescribed
interventions.rationale: Iron deficiency is associated with greater syndrome intensity

outcomes: Sleep pattern: achieve 6‑8 h of continuous sleep without >2 awakenings per night
Alertness: report energy level ≥ 7/10 during the day

interventions.action: Implement a relaxation routine (deep breathing, soft music) before bedtime
interventions.rationale: Reduces nervous system excitation and facilitates sleep onset

interventions.action: Limit caffeine and alcohol after 2:00 pm
interventions.rationale: These substances can exacerbate RLS symptoms and disturb sleep

interventions.action: Encourage moderate physical activity (30 min) at least 3 times per week
interventions.rationale: Regular exercise improves sleep quality and reduces RLS intensity

interventions.action: Review and document side effects of dopaminergic drugs (e.g., daytime sleepiness)
interventions.rationale: Allows medication adjustment to optimize sleep without excessive sedation

interventions.action: Coordinate with the physician for possible medication adjustment if episodes persist
interventions.rationale: Pharmacologic adjustments may be needed to control RLS and improve sleep

summary.0.quote: Restless legs syndrome (RLS) causes a powerful urge to move your legs.

key_points.4.quote: Depending on the patient, medication therapy for RLS may include iron, dopamine agonists (e.g., pramipexole, rotigotine, ropinirole), opioids, and benzodiazepines (NINDS, 2023).

sections.risk_factors.1.quote: Some conditions that may lead to RLS include neuropathy, pregnancy, renal disease/failure and hemodialysis (NINDS, 2023).

sections.risk_factors.3.quote: Caffeine, tobacco, and alcohol may make symptoms worse.

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: Some people describe it as a creeping, crawling, tingling, or burning sensation.

sections.signs_symptoms.2.quote: Moving makes your legs feel better, but not for long.

sections.signs_symptoms.3.quote: RLS tends to hinder falling asleep, but can also waken a person from sleep.

sections.treatment.1.quote: Depending on the patient, medication therapy for RLS may include iron, dopamine agonists (e.g., pramipexole, rotigotine, ropinirole), opioids, and benzodiazepines (NINDS, 2023).

sections.treatment.3.quote: Lifestyle changes, such as regular sleep habits, relaxation techniques, and moderate exercise during the day can help.

sections.complications.2.quote: Patients who have conditions and diseases such as migraines, lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, chronic back pain, irritable bowel syndrome, anxiety, and/or depression also tend to be more likely to develop fibromyalgia.

sections.nursing_care.3.quote: Lifestyle changes, such as regular sleep habits, relaxation techniques, and moderate exercise during the day can help.

sections.patient_teaching.2.quote: Lifestyle changes, such as regular sleep habits, relaxation techniques, and moderate exercise during the day can help.
